q-ap-01.The range sits unlevel, so the oven bake: Ask what the bracket physically holds in place, and whether a cooking complaint would make this a safety item at all.
q-ap-01.The bracket grounds the range, so withou: Think about what actually carries a ground path to an appliance frame. Is that a job for a metal bracket at the floor?
q-ap-01.It voids the manufacturer's warranty, wh: The stem asks about safety. A paperwork or warranty concern does not explain how anyone could get hurt.

q-ap-02.Operating the cooktop burners: Burners are the core job of a cooktop. Check what the SOP says about the basic functions of built-in appliances.
q-ap-02.Running the dishwasher through a complet: NC spells out how an installed dishwasher is run. Ask whether something the rule describes doing could also be excluded.
q-ap-02.Operating the range hood: Ask whether a range hood fan is a basic function of a built-in appliance, and what the SOP says about basic functions.

q-ap-03.To slow the drain so the pump does not r: Think about whether a loop in the hose changes how fast water flows, or does something else when the pump stops.
q-ap-03.To keep the hose from kinking where it b: A loop is a deliberate bend, so it is not there to prevent bends. Ask what the height of that loop accomplishes.
q-ap-03.To keep the hose up and away from the di: The loop's height is measured against the countertop, not the disposal's wiring. Ask what rising that high would stop.

q-ap-04.Through the drain cycle: Think about how many of the dishwasher's functions one phase alone would let you observe.
q-ap-04.Through a short rinse cycle: A short rinse saves time. Ask whether NC wrote this rule around saving the inspector time.
q-ap-04.Not operated; it is excluded: Built-in appliances get their basic functions checked under NC. Ask where an installed dishwasher falls.

q-ap-05.Major defect; a kitchen hood has to exha: Ask whether a design that manufacturers sell and install this way is a defect, or simply a different type of hood.
q-ap-05.Safety hazard; refer to an HVAC contract: Think about who gets hurt by a hood that filters instead of venting. Is that an injury risk, or a comfort difference?
q-ap-05.Not reportable, since the hood was worki: Ask whether reports describe only what works, or also what a system is and how it behaves for the client.

q-ap-06.Acceptable if the run is short and the d: A short, straight run helps airflow. Think about what else could happen in a duct carrying hot, lint-laden air.
q-ap-06.Acceptable as long as the lint filter is: A filter catches most lint, not all of it. Think about where the lint that slips past ends up over months.
q-ap-06.Cosmetic; suggest a neater rigid duct th: Ask whether the concern with this duct is how it looks, or what could happen inside it over years of drying.

q-ap-07.25 ft: 25 ft is the starting point. Ask what the two bends in the stem do to that number before calling it the maximum.
q-ap-07.20 ft: Check how much each 90 degree bend costs you, and make sure you counted both bends in the stem.
q-ap-07.10 ft: Check the deduction per 90 degree bend. You may have taken off more per bend than the course standard does.

q-ap-08.Into the attic, which is vented and carr: Attic vents move some air, but think about what warm, wet, lint-laden air does to framing over time.
q-ap-08.Into the crawlspace, below the insulatio: Crawlspaces already fight moisture. Ask what adding a dryer's output, every load, would do to the wood down there.
q-ap-08.Outdoors, through a hood with a fine scr: Pests are a fair worry. Ask what a fine mesh does after many loads of lint-laden air pass through it.

q-ap-09.Acceptable while it is not leaking; note: A bulge is not surface wear. Ask what has to give way inside a hose for it to swell under pressure.
q-ap-09.Not reportable, because a washer is not: You need not inspect a freestanding washer. Ask whether that stops you from mentioning a hazard you can plainly see.
q-ap-09.Note it as cosmetic wear on the hose cov: Cover wear stays flat. Think about what a bulge tells you about the layers holding back water pressure inside.

q-ap-10.Required to be inspected for temperature: Measuring temperature is a performance test. Ask whether the NC appliance section asks for performance numbers from anything.
q-ap-10.Required to be operated through a defros: A defrost cycle can take hours. Think about whether an SOP would ask you to run one during a visual inspection.
q-ap-10.Required if it is a built-in model: Ask whether being built in changes what kind of appliance a refrigerator is, under the NC exclusions.

q-ef-01.2 in of fall within the first 5 ft: Picture a heavy rain on that gentle slope. Would so little fall move water away before it soaks in at the wall?
q-ef-01.3 in of fall within the first 10 ft: Ask whether that much fall would keep water moving across grass and soil, or let it pool near the wall.
q-ef-01.12 in of fall within the first 3 ft: That is a steep bank right at the wall. Think about how far from the foundation the water needs to travel.

q-ef-02.The slope makes the lawn look uneven, wh: NC inspects grading for its effect on the building. Does how the lawn looks affect the building?
q-ef-02.Runoff will slowly erode the mulch beds: Ask whether the main concern here is landscaping, or something the inspection is actually responsible for.
q-ef-02.No concern; grading is outside the NC in: Check the NC exterior section: grading and drainage are named in it. Ask in what way they are inspected.

q-ef-03.1 in: Think about splashback and soil moisture. Would a finger's width keep the siding edge dry and termite trails visible?
q-ef-03.2 in: Picture rain splashing off mulch. Ask whether 2 in leaves room to see termite tubes and keep the wall base dry.
q-ef-03.12 in: You may be thinking of a larger figure from another rule. Recheck the minimum taught for siding above soil.

q-ef-04.Determine its R-value and note whether i: Ask whether an inspector can see behind finished cladding, and whether insulation value is a cladding duty at all.
q-ef-04.Probe the vinyl panels with an awl to ch: Probing is for a material that can rot. Ask whether vinyl decays the way wood does.
q-ef-04.Inspect it and report on safety glazing: Recall NC's exterior exclusions. Ask whether safety glazing is something NC asks you to report.

q-ef-05.Vinyl is the waterproof layer, so a crac: Recheck the stem: it says vinyl is not the main water barrier. Does this option agree with that?
q-ef-05.The crack is cosmetic, but buyers expect: Ask whether a crack only changes how the wall looks, or also changes how the wall system performs over time.
q-ef-05.Cracked vinyl gives off fumes in the sun: Ask whether there is any evidence behind a health claim like this, and what the siding's real job on the wall is.

q-ef-06.Major defect; refer to a structural engi: Ask what an engineer would find in cracks with no displacement. What would make a crack structural?
q-ef-06.Safety hazard; the cracks will become a: The stem says no trip edge exists. Ask whether you report a hazard that is not there.
q-ef-06.Repair; recommend sealing or replacing t: Ask whether hairline cracks from curing are something to fix, or something concrete normally does.

q-ef-07.Hairline cracks running across the full: Ask whether how far a crack runs tells you anything about safety, or whether something else matters more.
q-ef-07.Oil and rust stains near the garage that: Stains change how concrete looks. Ask whether that affects anyone's safety or the building itself.
q-ef-07.Concrete that has darkened and weathered: Ask whether color and age by themselves change how the driveway performs or how safe it is to walk on.

q-ef-08.For landscaping quality and the health o: Ask whether a home inspector is trained to judge plant health, and why the SOP would mention vegetation at all.
q-ef-08.For compliance with the local storm wate: A home inspection is not a code or ordinance inspection. Ask what the SOP does want from you here.
q-ef-08.Not inspected, since site work is outsid: Check NC .1107: vegetation, grading, and drainage are named in it. So ask how they are inspected, not whether.

q-ef-09.8 in, or 6 in where masonry veneer is us: Recheck the model IRC minimum. You may be carrying a larger number over from another clearance rule.
q-ef-09.4 in, or 2 in where brick veneer is used: Think about what exposed foundation does: keeps wood off wet soil and shows termite tubes. Would 2 in do that?
q-ef-09.12 in, or 8 in where masonry veneer is u: A foot of exposed wall is generous. Ask whether the IRC minimum is really set that high.

q-eh-01.Acceptable; gutters are a maintenance it: Recall what NC says about roof drainage. Are gutters part of the system you must inspect?
q-eh-01.Major defect; recommend replacing the gu: Ask whether these gutters failed by being too small, or whether something is filling them.
q-eh-01.Monitor and recheck after the next heavy: The stem already shows the problem: leaves and plants. Ask what waiting for rain would tell you that you do not know now.

q-eh-02.Acceptable; downspouts are designed to e: Think about how much roof area drains into one downspout, and where all that water goes when it lands at the wall.
q-eh-02.Recommend removing the downspout so wate: Ask whether spreading roof water along the eave keeps it off the foundation, or just spreads the problem around the house.
q-eh-02.Not reportable, since the gutter system: A working gutter collects water. Ask whether the system has finished its job once water reaches the downspout.

q-eh-03.Both standards require testing the seal: Ask whether testing every seal fits a visual inspection, and compare what each SOP actually lists for windows.
q-eh-03.Neither standard lets you mention fogged: Ask whether an SOP ever forbids reporting something you plainly see. Exclusions limit your duty, not what you may say.
q-eh-03.NC requires reporting it and recommendin: Check which SOP is which. You may have given NC a duty that comes from a different standard.

q-eh-04.It sits level so water can drain off bot: Ask where water draining off the inside of a sill would end up, and whether you want any of it going there.
q-eh-04.It slopes inward toward the sash so rain: Follow a raindrop down that slope. Where does it end up, and what sits at the bottom of the slope?
q-eh-04.It relies on paint alone, so no sealant: Paint protects the wood surface. Ask whether it can also seal a joint between two pieces of trim.

q-eh-05.You report it as a code violation and ci: A home inspection is not a code inspection. Ask whether NC wants you citing plumbing code here.
q-eh-05.You recommend a backflow test by the wat: Think about scale: is a utility backflow test the usual next step for one hose bib at an inspection?
q-eh-05.It is excluded, so you leave it out of t: An exclusion means you need not do something. Ask whether it also forbids reporting a risk you notice.

q-eh-06.A pipe that crosses another pipe without: The name sounds like pipe layout. Ask why NC would bother to define two pipes touching without a fitting.
q-eh-06.A direct connection between the hot and: Ask what harm a hot to cold link would do. Is that a health risk, or a comfort and control problem?
q-eh-06.Two fixture drains that share one trap u: Drains carry waste out of the house. Ask which side of the plumbing a cross connection rule protects.

q-eh-07.Acceptable; exterior entry steps are exe: Ask whether a fall on outdoor steps hurts less than one indoors. Why would entry steps get an exemption?
q-eh-07.Acceptable; a handrail is required start: Recheck the riser count that triggers a handrail. Is it the number you remember, or a different one?
q-eh-07.Acceptable, because concrete steps do no: Ask whether the material a step is made of changes how a person falls on it.

q-eh-08.30 to 34 in above the tread nosings: Picture bracing a fall on the way down. This range sits a bit low for most adult hands; recheck it.
q-eh-08.36 to 42 in above the tread nosings: You may be blending handrail height with guard height. Ask which one this range belongs to.
q-eh-08.28 to 32 in above the tread nosings: Think about where an adult's hand rests when walking down stairs. Would this range help someone catch a fall?

q-eh-09.Decks and appurtenant railings: Decks carry people and can fail. Ask whether NC would leave out an attached structure that people stand on.
q-eh-09.Entryway doors: Entry doors are part of the house itself. Check the required list in .1107 before calling them excluded.
q-eh-09.Eaves, soffits, and fascias: These trim the roof edge and help keep water out of the house. Check whether .1107 names them as required.

q-eh-10.Step (sidewall) flashing: Step flashing works along the sidewall. Ask what happens to the water at the very end of that run.
q-eh-10.Drip edge (eave) flashing: Drip edge lines the eave, not a wall. Ask where the stem's roof edge meets the house.
q-eh-10.Valley (open metal) flashing: Valleys form where two roof planes meet. Does the stem describe two roof planes, or a roof against a wall?

q-fp-01.12 in in front and 6 in on each side: Ask whether this extension would catch a rolling log. Recheck the figures for openings under 6 sq ft.
q-fp-01.20 in in front and 12 in on each side: Those figures belong to bigger openings. Check where the size cutoff falls and which side of it 5 sq ft sits on.
q-fp-01.8 in in front and 4 in on each side: Picture an ember popping out onto the floor. Would 8 in of hearth in front catch it?

q-fp-02.It is cosmetic, though the client may wa: Ask whether gaps in the part of the house that holds the fire are a looks issue or a job issue.
q-fp-02.It mainly weakens the draft, so smoke ma: Ask what the firebox's own job is, and whether draft is the first thing that job protects.
q-fp-02.Firebox masonry is excluded, so report i: Check whether the SOP really excludes the firebox, or whether you are thinking of the flue interior.

q-fp-03.Leave it alone; dampers are outside the: Ask whether moving a readily accessible handle is beyond a visual inspection, or part of it.
q-fp-03.Remove the damper plate so you can inspe: Ask whether removing parts fits a visual inspection, or belongs to a chimney sweep.
q-fp-03.Close it and tape it shut for safety unt: Think about what happens if someone lights a fire under a damper that has been sealed shut. Is that safer?

q-fp-04.Stage 1, sooty and brushable: Sooty deposits are soft and powdery. Ask whether shiny and hard describes something a brush would sweep off.
q-fp-04.Stage 2, crunchy and flaky: Crunchy flakes break apart under a tool. Does the stem's description sound like that texture?
q-fp-04.It is not creosote, just heat discolorat: Discoloration is a color change in the surface. Ask whether a tar-like deposit you can see is just color.

q-fp-05.A Level I visual inspection by the homeo: Ask who is qualified to inspect a chimney at sale, and how much a basic homeowner look could show.
q-fp-05.A smoke test performed by the home inspe: The stem says your SOP does not require the flue interior. Ask whether testing the flue fits your role.
q-fp-05.No recommendation; the flue is outside t: Outside the SOP means not required, not off limits. Ask how you would help a client cover that gap.

q-fp-06.3 ft from the ridge, 2 ft from walls, 10: Ask what problem a chimney rule like this solves. Would trees and walls be the main thing it measures against?
q-fp-06.3 ft wide, 2 ft deep, and 10 ft tall at: These sound like sizing numbers. Ask whether the 3-2-10 rule is about the chimney's size or its position.
q-fp-06.3 in clearance, 2 in air space, and a 10: Check the units. Ask whether this rule is measured in inches or in feet.

q-fp-07.It holds the spark arrestor screen and t: Spark arrestors and rain caps are their own part. Ask what the crown's job is by itself.
q-fp-07.It narrows the flue outlet at the top to: Ask whether choking a flue outlet would help or hurt draft, and whether the crown sits in the gas path at all.
q-fp-07.It is decorative trim that hides the top: Think about the top of the masonry through rain and freeze-thaw. Is the crown only there for looks?

q-fp-08.Nothing; caps are decorative and optiona: Ask what an open flue top lets in when no fire is burning, over many seasons.
q-fp-08.The fireplace should not be used until a: Ask whether a missing cap changes how a fire burns today. Is it really a stop-use condition?
q-fp-08.The chimney needs to be rebuilt with a t: A taller flue addresses draft. Does the stem describe a draft problem, or something missing at the top?

q-fp-09.A kickout flashing to turn water into th: Kickouts work at a roof edge beside a wall. Is this chimney at a roof edge, or out on the slope?
q-fp-09.A wider apron flashing to spread water a: Ask where an apron flashing sits on a chimney, and whether that is the side the stem is asking about.
q-fp-09.Nothing extra, if the step flashing is s: Ask whether the chimney width in the stem triggers an extra requirement under the course standard.

q-fp-10.1/2 in: Think about years of heat conducting through brick. Would half an inch let it dissipate before the wood suffers?
q-fp-10.1 in: You may be recalling the figure for a chimney outside the exterior walls. Where does the stem put this one?
q-fp-10.6 in: Ask whether you are borrowing the clearance taught for single-wall metal vent connectors instead of masonry.

q-fp-11.The damper opening creates suction that: A damper is an opening you control. Ask whether an opening can create pull on its own.
q-fp-11.Wind blowing across the chimney top pull: Ask whether a chimney still draws on a still, windless night. If it does, what drives it?
q-fp-11.The firebox's sloped back wall forces th: Ask whether a short sloped wall in the firebox could push smoke up a whole flue on its own.

q-hv-01.Filters are excluded, but a dirty one is: Check NC's list of heating distribution items. Ask whether air filters appear on that list.
q-hv-01.The furnace safety switch will lock out: Ask whether every furnace has a switch tied to filter condition, or whether that is a guess.
q-hv-01.A dirty filter makes the furnace produce: Carbon monoxide comes from combustion problems. Ask whether the filter sits on the combustion side or the air side.

q-hv-02.Downward toward the chimney at least 1/4: Hot gases rise. Ask which way a pipe should run to let them do what they naturally do.
q-hv-02.Level, so the gases flow evenly into the: Ask what hot gases do in a flat pipe once they start to cool. Does level help them move along?
q-hv-02.Upward toward the chimney at least 1 in: Recheck the minimum rise per foot. You may be remembering a larger figure than the one usually taught.

q-hv-03.Acceptable; 2 in is the standard clearan: Ask whether you are thinking of a double-wall vent. Does the pipe in the stem run cooler or hotter than that?
q-hv-03.Acceptable as long as the joist shows no: Ask whether heat damage to wood always shows today, or can build up over years of exposure.
q-hv-03.Not reportable, since vent clearances ar: Ask whether you can stay silent about a fire risk you can see and measure, even when a trade fixes it.

q-hv-04.Inspect the heat exchanger with a mirror: Check the NC exclusions at the furnace. Ask whether heat exchangers are something you must inspect.
q-hv-04.Relight the pilot if it is out so the fu: Ask whether lighting a pilot is an inspector's task under NC, or something left to the owner or a technician.
q-hv-04.Determine whether each room gets enough: Ask whether you can judge heat adequacy in one visit. Check whether NC lists it among exclusions.

q-hv-05.Its temperature at the time of the inspe: A temperature on inspection day changes by the hour. Ask what fixed fact about the room NC wants recorded.
q-hv-05.The BTU rating needed to heat that room': Sizing a system is an engineering calculation. Ask whether NC asks home inspectors for load numbers.
q-hv-05.Whether the room's thermostat is calibra: Recall what NC excludes about calibration elsewhere in the SOP. Ask whether this would be required room by room.

q-hv-06.The smaller liquid line, since it carrie: On a running condenser, ask which line feels warm to the touch and which feels cool. Which one would sweat?
q-hv-06.Neither, since both lines run near the o: Touch both lines on a running system. Ask whether they really feel the same temperature as the outdoor air.
q-hv-06.The condensate drain line running from t: The stem asks about refrigerant lines at the condenser. Ask whether a condensate drain is one of those.

q-hv-07.It is cosmetic, though the pad should be: Ask whether a leaning machine only looks off, or also stresses the parts connected to it.
q-hv-07.It mainly makes the fan louder, which ne: Noise is a nuisance. Ask whether there is a mechanical reason a tilted unit would be a concern.
q-hv-07.Not reportable, since the condenser itse: Ask whether NC's cooling section really leaves out the outdoor unit, or whether that is an assumption.

q-hv-08.At the main panel, labeled for the conde: Picture a technician at the condenser. Could they see whether someone flips that breaker back on?
q-hv-08.Inside the house, near the thermostat th: Ask who needs to control the disconnect, and where that person is standing while they work.
q-hv-08.Anywhere along the same circuit as the c: Ask whether a disconnect the technician cannot find or see would protect them while their hands are in the unit.

q-hv-09.32 F: Freezing is a common cutoff. Ask whether a compressor is safe to run on a cool day well above freezing.
q-hv-09.50 F: Recheck the InterNACHI figure. Ask whether a compressor could be harmed on a day many people would call mild.
q-hv-09.75 F: That is a warm day. Ask whether a cutoff that high would leave cooling untested for much of the year.

q-hv-10.Returns mainly matter in winter, when th: Ask whether the same blower and ducts move air in summer too. Is the return part of both seasons?
q-hv-10.Returns are mostly decorative grilles th: Ask what would happen to airflow if you taped over every return grille in the house.
q-hv-10.Returns carry exhaust gases out of the l: Ask whether combustion gases ever enter the house air ducts by design, or leave through a flue.

q-hv-11.Acceptable, because the vented attic wil: Ask what the room below loses, and what cold air does in a warm attic, before calling it acceptable.
q-hv-11.Cosmetic; reattach it with tape the next: Ask whether a disconnected duct is about looks, or about where the air the owner pays to condition ends up.
q-hv-11.Not reportable, since attic ductwork is: Ask whether NC's heating and cooling sections cover distribution, and whether ducts are part of distribution.

q-wh-01.12 in: Picture scalding water leaving a pipe at knee height. Who could it hit on the way down?
q-wh-01.18 in: You may be thinking of the garage ignition height. Recheck the TPR termination figure.
q-wh-01.24 in: Ask how far scalding water sprays when it leaves a pipe that high, and who might be standing nearby.

q-wh-02.Pipe the same size as the valve outlet: Ask whether a pipe that matches the valve outlet is a problem, or whether a reduction in size would be.
q-wh-02.Termination 4 in above the floor: Recall the maximum height above the floor for the termination. Is 4 in inside that limit or outside it?
q-wh-02.Pipe running downhill by gravity in the: Ask which way water should flow in a discharge pipe so nothing traps it along the way.

q-wh-03.The tank wall is thickest there and prot: Ask whether the probe is placed for its own protection, or to sense something about the water.
q-wh-03.The cold water inlet is at the top of th: Ask what the probe is meant to sense. Would sitting beside incoming cold water help it do that?
q-wh-03.It keeps the probe clear of sediment at: Ask whether avoiding sediment explains a rule about the top 6 in specifically, rather than just staying off the bottom.

q-wh-04.Gas collects inside the tank and ignites: Ask what is actually stored inside the tank under pressure. Is it gas?
q-wh-04.Sediment reacts with the steel lining an: Ask whether there is any explosive chemistry between sediment and steel, or whether you are guessing at a cause.
q-wh-04.Cold water hitting the hot steel cracks: Ask whether a steel tank behaves like glass, and what stored energy inside it could be released when it fails.

q-wh-05.You are required to estimate the remaini: Check NC's exclusions about life expectancy. Ask whether an estimate is a required item.
q-wh-05.You are required to recommend replacing: Ask whether age alone is a defect, or information the client can use for planning.
q-wh-05.You may not mention the age, since that: An exclusion limits what you must report. Ask whether it also forbids sharing useful context.

q-wh-06.6 in: You may be thinking of the TPR discharge figure. Ask where gasoline vapor collects in a garage.
q-wh-06.12 in: Gasoline vapor is heavier than air. Ask whether 12 in clears the layer that pools near the floor.
q-wh-06.36 in: Ask whether the rule really requires that much height, or whether you are adding a safety margin of your own.

q-wh-07.It drains condensed water out of the bot: Ask which system the drip leg belongs to. Is it on the tank's water side or on the gas supply?
q-wh-07.It slows the gas flow so the burner ligh: Ask whether a short capped pipe off the line could meter gas flow. What else could it do?
q-wh-07.It works as a second shutoff valve right: A shutoff has a handle or valve. Ask whether a drip leg has any way to stop the flow.

q-wh-08.Normal heat from a draft hood that is wo: Ask whether scorching is ever normal on a working appliance. What would have to escape to cause it?
q-wh-08.The thermostat is set too high and the b: Ask whether water temperature inside the tank would scorch the outside top, right at the draft hood.
q-wh-08.The TPR valve has discharged steam onto: Ask whether steam leaves scorch marks or water and rust stains, and where the TPR pipe sends its discharge.

q-wh-09.Yes; NC requires testing it as part of t: Check NC's plumbing exclusions about automatic safety controls before deciding testing is required.
q-wh-09.Yes, if the client is present to watch t: Ask whether having a witness changes what can happen to an old valve after you lift its lever.
q-wh-09.Yes, if the tank is under 10 years old a: Ask whether age and a drain pan change your duty under NC, or only change how a leak gets caught.

q-wh-10.Its age, remaining life, and the conditi: Ask whether NC requires life expectancy, and whether an anode rod is visible without taking things apart.
q-wh-10.Its recovery rate in gallons per hour an: Ask whether NC asks you to judge capacity adequacy or performance at all during a visual inspection.
q-wh-10.Whether a thermal expansion tank is pres: Check NC's water heater exclusions. Ask whether expansion tanks are on the required list or the excluded one.

q-mo-01.Report nothing, since a dry reading show: Ask what a dry reading proves about the next storm, or a leak that only shows up in certain weather.
q-mo-01.Report it as an active leak and refer to: Ask whether a dry reading supports calling the leak active, and whether you know the source is the roof.
q-mo-01.Recommend replacing the roof covering ab: Ask whether one stain, reading dry, justifies a roof replacement before anyone has found the source.

q-mo-02.That the drywall behind the cool spot is: Ask what else besides water can make a ceiling spot read cool on a thermal camera.
q-mo-02.That mold is growing on the back side of: Ask whether a camera that sees surface temperature could tell you anything about what is growing out of sight.
q-mo-02.That the insulation above that spot is m: Missing insulation is one possible cause. Ask whether it is the only thing that could read cool.

q-mo-03.8 percent: Ask where dry framing lumber usually reads. Could a decay threshold sit that low?
q-mo-03.12 percent: Ask whether that figure is a warning level, or closer to where normal dry lumber sits.
q-mo-03.50 percent: Ask whether decay waits until wood is that soaked, or can start at a much lower reading.

q-mo-04.Acceptable; sink cabinets often get wet: Ask whether normal use would swell a cabinet floor and leave it reading wet.
q-mo-04.Recommend replacing the countertop and s: Ask whether you know the source yet, and whether the counter is what got damaged.
q-mo-04.Monitor it and recheck the reading after: Ask whether a swollen particleboard floor that reads wet today needs more evidence before you act.

q-mo-05.It is cosmetic, though buyers notice a s: Ask what the caulk joint is there to stop, and where water goes when the joint opens.
q-mo-05.It mainly affects how the grout looks al: Caulk and grout are different materials with different jobs. Ask what this particular joint's job is.
q-mo-05.Caulk is outside the NC SOP, but it is a: Ask whether the SOP really excludes caulk, or whether you are assuming small items are out of scope.

q-mo-06.Normal moisture after a recent shower, s: Look at the pattern in the stem. Would shower splash leave one wet spot with dry tile all around it?
q-mo-06.A failed shower pan liner, which you sho: Ask whether NC asks you to test shower pan liners, and whether a soap dish sits where a pan would be.
q-mo-06.Mold behind the tile, which you should i: Check NC's exclusions on environmental conditions. Ask whether naming mold is part of your job.

q-mo-07.A cracked tank lid dripping onto the flo: A lid sits on top of the tank and holds no water. Ask what a cracked lid could drip.
q-mo-07.Condensation from the tank on a humid da: Condensation could wet the floor. Ask whether it explains the toilet rocking.
q-mo-07.A clogged vent stack forcing water back: Ask whether a vent problem explains the toilet itself rocking on the floor.

q-mo-08.As mold growth that needs remediation by: Check NC's exclusions on mold and other environmental conditions. Can you name a stain as mold?
q-mo-08.As acceptable, since crawlspace wood oft: Compare 24 percent with the reading commonly treated as elevated for wood. Which side of it does this joist sit on?
q-mo-08.As a structural failure of the joist; re: Ask whether the stem describes sagging, cracking, or failure, or only moisture and staining.

q-mo-09.The duct is leaking water that drains fr: Supply ducts carry air, not condensate. Ask where water on the outside of the duct is coming from.
q-mo-09.The duct is too warm, so it draws water: Check the stem: it says a cold supply duct. Ask which way temperature has to go for air to give up water.
q-mo-09.Rainwater is entering through the founda: Ask whether rain entering vents explains water forming on the duct itself, all along its length.

q-mo-10.The two stains are unrelated, and each o: Ask how likely it is that two wet stains line up exactly, one above the other, by chance.
q-mo-10.The ceiling drywall below has to be repl: Ask whether the question is about repair scope, or about what the attic stain tells you.
q-mo-10.Nothing reportable, since the attic shea: Ask whether NC leaves attic sheathing out, or asks you to report how the attic was inspected.
